title: Define error-class-driven rollback contracts and runbook scenarios for serving degradations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: After a recent set of KV-cache-related incidents and a kernel-level regression that caused disproportionate tail latency, we need to codify a set of deterministic rollback contracts and accompanying runbook scenarios tied to specific error classes. The goal is to reduce mean time to mitigation for common, recurring failure classes and to make PRD acceptance criteria testable and automatable. This ticket translates postmortem action items into product requirements: error-class taxonomy, explicit rollback actions, operator runbooks, and automated acceptance checks.
background: Postmortem(s) referenced: KV-cache regen outage 2026-01-27 (INC-2026-011) and kernel regression spike 2026-02-03 (INC-2026-017). Root causes included: cache rehydration storms, unbounded batching causing kernel OOMs, and an aggressive kernel selector rollout. Operators performed manual traffic shepherding and model variant fallbacks. Postmortem action items recommended encoding decision trees into the PRD and implementing synthetic verification for runbook triggers.
postmortem_reference: INC-2026-011: KV cache regen storm postmortem (link: https://confluence.redwood/INC-2026-011)
goals: Create an error-class taxonomy for serving degradations (e.g., KV_CACHE_STALL, KERNEL_OOM, TAIL_LATENCY_SPIKE, MODEL_FALLBACK_ERRORS)
Define deterministic rollback contracts (what to rollback to, when, and who approves)
Ship operator runbooks with step-by-step decision trees and automation hooks
Add PRD acceptance criteria that are verifiable by synthetic canaries and unit tests
Ensure telemetry and alert tags are emitted to drive automated rollback triggers
requirements: Taxonomy: Product and SRE agree on a canonical list of error classes, severity mapping, and signal thresholds

Contracts: For each error class, define primary mitigation, fallback path, and rollback criteria (e.g., if KERNEL_OOM >= 3 occurrences in 10m AND tail latency > 250ms, then rollback kernel to previous stable build)
Runbooks: Author playbooks for on-call and runbooks automation with clear operator checks and rollback command examples
Automation hooks: Define observable signals (metrics/logs/trace attributes) and implement a controller that can propose rollbacks (requires human approval for P1 by default)
Acceptance tests: Synthetic scenarios that simulate each error class and assert that the system either declares 'mitigated' or triggers the defined rollback within target time windows
Docs: Link to updated PRD sections and operator-facing docs in Console and Runbook repository
acceptance_criteria: A canonical error-class list is published in the PRD and linked from Console incident pages
For at least four prioritized error classes (KV_CACHE_STALL, KERNEL_OOM, TAIL_LATENCY_SPIKE, MODEL_SERVING_TIMEOUT) there are written rollback contracts and operator checklists
Automation: A synthetic canary run simulating KV_CACHE_STALL triggers the rollback proposer and, after simulated human approval, triggers the rollback in a staging environment within 10 minutes
Tests: CI job 'rollback-contracts-e2e' runs and validates decision tree branches for all four classes with pass/fail signals
Telemetry: Alerts include the error_class label and a severity tag and appear on the same dashboard used by SRE and PM
Operator training: Two runbook drills conducted with on-call and PM present; drill notes and gaps recorded in the PRD
in_scope: Implementing synthetic canaries for the prioritized error classes in staging
Updating Console runbook links and incident page metadata
Adding metric/label requirements to telemetry instrumentation backlog
out_of_scope: Automating rollbacks without human approval for P1 incidents
Rewriting kernel selection logic (this ticket only defines rollback contracts)
Large-scale infra changes (e.g., changing autoscaler design)
risks: Overly aggressive rollback criteria could cause unnecessary churn and increased customer impact
Incomplete telemetry labels may lead to false positives/negatives in automation triggers
Operator friction if runbooks are too verbose or lack clear owner steps
metrics: Mean time to rollback decision (target: < 12 minutes for P1 after alert)
Number of incidents mitigated via defined rollback contract vs ad-hoc operator action (target: 75% automated proposal rate)
False positive rollback proposals in staging (target: < 3% per synthetic run)
Runbook drill pass rate (target: 2/2 drills with no major gaps)
dependencies: SRE: finalize signal definitions and thresholds
Runtime: expose error_class labels on traces and metrics
Console: add incident page hooks to surface PRD-defined runbooks
CI/QA: create synthetic canary harness and gating tests
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Align taxonomy with SRE and runtime (2 weeks). Phase 2: Draft rollback contracts and operator runbooks; ship to staging with synthetic canaries (3 weeks). Phase 3: Runbook drills and iterate; gate release on CI e2e pass and two successful runbook drills (2 weeks). Phase 4: Gradual rollout to production with monitoring and 72h hypercare.
test_plan: Unit tests for decision tree logic (CI)
Synthetic canary jobs per error class that assert proposer and rollback sequence
Staging drill with simulated alerts and human approvals
Post-release smoke tests to ensure alerts surface expected labels
prs: GH PR: runtime: add error_class label -> https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1248
GH PR: console: incident metadata link -> https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/879
notes: Design decision: human approval required for P0/P1 to avoid accidental mass rollbacks; automation may auto-apply for P2/P3 if explicitly enabled per-tenant
Consideration: tie rollback contracts to release metadata (git hash) so we can do targeted reverts
Follow-up: evaluate adding an automated 'rollback dry-run' mode that performs all checks without executing changes
